Subject: MSA + Order Form: liability allocation for security incident

Hi Priya / Ben,

Thanks for the draft MSA and the early walkthrough last week. Our legal team ran a quick pass and raised a couple of items we need to resolve before procurement can approve:

1) Liability cap — we need a clearly defined per-incident sublimit for security events tied to the Security Addendum. Given the sensitivity of PHI, our counsel is asking that for any confirmed data security incident involving regulated data the per-incident cap be set at $10,000,000.
2) Carve-outs — they want the usual carve-outs to include gross negligence and willful misconduct (we expect Redwood to accept), but are pushing for an exception for breaches of encryption/misuse clauses.
3) Consequential damages — Greenbank insists on preserving consequential damages for third-party fines and regulator penalties resulting from breaches.

Can Redwood provide suggested language that (a) ties the sublimit explicitly to the Security Addendum, (b) clarifies whether it is per-incident or aggregate, and (c) states whether regulatory fines are carved out from the cap?

Attached is a short spreadsheet with the redline points. Happy to do a call if easier.

Best,
Samantha

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FW: MSA + Order Form: liability allocation for security incident

Team — high level legal take below.

Summary: Redwood's standard MSA cap is 1x fees (12-month trailing) with carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct. For security events we have a Security Addendum that provides incident definitions, notification timelines, and controls.

Recommendation for negotiation:
- Tie a security-event sublimit explicitly to Section 4.A of the Security Addendum.
- Offer a per-incident sublimit equal to the greater of (i) 3x the annual fees paid under the Order Form or (ii) $5,000,000. This preserves commercial predictability while acknowledging PHI sensitivity.
- Carve-outs: keep gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap; do NOT carve regulator fines or statutory penalties out of the cap by default — instead propose a limited carve-out for third-party civil fines that are the direct result of Redwood's documented failure to follow mandatory encryption/segregation commitments in the Security Addendum, subject to proof and mitigation.
- Consequential damages: continue Redwood's standard exclusion for consequential damages but propose an explicit limited exception for direct regulatory fines where the incident was caused by Redwood's material breach of security obligations. Even then cap recoverable regulatory fines to the per-incident sublimit.

Draft redline: "For any Security Event (as defined in the Security Addendum), the liability of Redwood for damages arising solely from such Security Event shall be limited to the greater of (a) three times the annual fees paid under the applicable Order Form and (b) $5,000,000 (the 'Security Event Sublimit'). Notwithstanding the foregoing, damages resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct are not limited. Regulatory fines and statutory penalties shall be recoverable only to the extent they arise from Redwood's material breach of obligations set forth in the Security Addendum and, even if recoverable, shall be subject to the Security Event Sublimit."

Commercial note: $5M floor provides a middle ground vs their $10M ask. It keeps exposure bounded while giving the customer a per-incident metric. If Ben/Priya believe this is a BAU kill for Greenbank, we can escalate to Head of Revenue for exception authority.

I'll attach a redline to the MSA and a Security Addendum excerpt for the customer.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Redwood_MSA_redline_v2.docx; Redwood_Security_Addendum_v1.3.pdf)

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: liability allocation for security incident

Hi Samantha — thanks for the details and for the spreadsheet. Our legal team reviewed and we have a proposed compromise to present:

1) Security Event Sublimit (per-incident): greater of (i) 3x annual fees or (ii) $5M.
2) Carve-outs: gross negligence and willful misconduct remain outside the cap; regulator fines will only be recoverable to the extent they directly result from Redwood's documented material breach of the specific controls in the Security Addendum, and any such recoverable fines are subject to the Security Event Sublimit.
3) Consequential damages: we maintain the standard exclusion for consequential damages; however, direct regulatory fines tied to Redwood's material failure are captured as in (2).

We attached a redline copy of the MSA and the Security Addendum excerpt that ties the sublimit to the Addendum. Optionally we can present an enhanced monitoring & contractually-backed runbook for PHI customers as additional commercial comfort.

Would Greenbank consider the 3x/5M compromise? If not, please indicate whether a $7.5M per-incident floor would be acceptable, or if the $10M is non-negotiable. Happy to jump on a call today at 3pm PT.

Best,
Priya
(Attachment: Redwood_MSA_redline_v2.docx; Redwood_Security_Addendum_v1.3.pdf)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@greenbankhealth.com>

Cc: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@greenbankhealth.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: liability allocation for security incident

Priya,

Appreciate the quick turn. We reviewed Laura's proposal internally. A few clarifications and pushes from Greenbank counsel:

- $5M floor is lower than counsel's tolerance for PHI exposure. They will not accept anything below $8M as a per-incident minimum.
- The carve-out language tying regulator fines to "material breach of obligations set forth in the Security Addendum" is too narrow. Counsel wants regulator fines for data breaches involving PHI to be compensable outside the cap or, at a minimum, subject to a separate higher sublimit.
- They reiterated that consequential damages related to third-party regulator penalties cannot be fully excluded in our vertical — they expect a tailored exception.

Greenbank is open to a middle path: per-incident sublimit of $8M + a separate carve-out for regulator penalties capped at $15M, but they would prefer unlimited recoveries for statutory penalties (which is non-starter for us).

We can discuss on the 3pm PT call if you confirm.

Thanks,
Samantha

Subject: Internal: Greenbank negotiation update and next steps

Quick internal update after today's call with Samantha/Tom:

- Customer stance: firm on at least $8M per-incident floor and wants a separate regulator penalty bucket (they floated $15M) or unlimited statutory recoveries (we said no).
- Legal recommendation remains the 3x / $5M floor but Laura is ok to present an escalation path: (i) elevate to Head of Revenue for a final commercial exception up to $8M per incident but only with a split-risk approach (customer takes first $3M, Redwood takes next $5M), and (ii) regulator fines treated as recoverable only where Redwood's specific security controls in the Addendum were violated, with a negotiated separate cap (not unlimited).
- Commercial ask: Ben / Priya to confirm whether sales can accept a split-risk structure or we should push for $5M + enhanced controls and monitoring commitments. If Greenbank insists on a $15M regulator bucket, we should require a high-value security escrow and quarterly compliance attestations; otherwise reject.

Next steps: Ben will discuss escalation to Head of Revenue; Laura will prepare two final redline options (1: legal standard compromise — 3x/5M; 2: escalated commercial exception — split-risk up to $8M plus limited regulator cap). Priya will present both options on call with customer tomorrow.

Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
